3. The High Court Division observed that the certificate issued under Section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in respect of 'Ka' schedule properties in favour of the decree holder Bank by Annexure-B and the subsequent order dated 25. 11. 2007 (Annexure to- "E") rejecting the application of the judgment- debtor to repay the entire outstanding decretal dues by selling the mortgaged property by the judgment debtor can be declared illegal by the Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat under Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain as the Court is not powerless. 

 5. The learned Counsel for the appellant submitted that the judgment and summary order and observation of the High Court Division is misconceived and barred by Section 5(4) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 as the decree of foreclosure in favour of the plaintiff has been issued under Section 5(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain and the decree attained its finality. The judgment debtor shall have no right to I redeem the said mortgaged property and as such the judgment of the High Court Division is had in law and is liable to be set aside. He further submitted that the High Court Division manifestly erred in law and committed gross illegally in observing that the executing court can consider the application under Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain after finality of the decree and it's executing as the Artha Rin Adalat Ain after issuance of certificate under Section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain became funtus officio and the impugned judgment is an apparent error of law resulting in an error in the decision as such order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. He also further submitted that the High Court Division misconceived and misconstrued Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain as the inherent power of the Artha Rin Adalat can be exercised only when the Adalat is in sisin of the matter and to prevent the misuse of process of the Court but in the present case the Artha Rin Adalat became funtus officio and in such direction to the Artha Rin Adalat to re-consider and re-open a past and closed matter is rather an abuse of process of the Court and as such the judgment of the High Court Division is illegal and misconceived and liable to be set aside. He lastly submitted that in passing the impugned order, the High Court Division did not take into consideration that the suit property had already been mutated in the name of the petitioner after registration of the sale deed and unless and until the said sale deed is cancelled by a competent civil Court, the same will remain valid in law, and as such the impugned judgment and order is violative of the legal and constitutional right of the appellant and as such the same is liable to be set aside. 

 7. It appears that the decree of foreclosure in favour of the plaintiff attained its finality and the judgment debtor shall have no right to redeem the said mortgaged property. Moreover after issuance of the certificate under Section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain the same court of Artha Rin Adalat Ain had no power to entertain the application of the appellant invoking Section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain as such power under Section 57 is only available when the other provisions of the Ain are not exhaustive. In this case after the certificate issued under Section 33(5) of the AM the decree-holder has already sold the suit property in favour of the respondent No. 8, Md. Rafique by registered sale deed and therefore there is no scope to interfere with the bonafide purchase for value.
